title: Case debrief: 'oil drives coffee' — answer the claim
rubric: Identifies the result as a spurious regression: two trending, non-stationary prices; the levels R² and t-stat are not valid evidence (≈ 9 in 10 independent random-walk pairs look significant).
Quotes the decisive check: in daily changes the relationship vanishes (returns correlation ≈ 0.03, t ≈ 0.8, R² ≈ 0.001).
Separates correlation from causality: even a genuine correlation would not show that oil drives coffee (common factors such as the dollar or general commodity flows, reverse causality, coincidence).
Distinguishes statistical significance from economic significance and from predictive value.

Takes the economic story seriously but says what evidence it would need: a mechanism with a plausible size and lag, a link in changes, a stable relationship across sub-periods, and a cointegration test if a level relationship is claimed.
Contrasts with Brent–WTI, where the link survives in differences and there is an arbitrage mechanism — the methodology is the same, the outcome differs.
